summary_md:
**Shawn Bang ([@wushi123321](https://x.com/wushi123321/status/2115641269406093385))** covers Cloudflare's open-sourced **security-audit-skill**, the skill behind its internal bug-hunting harness: point a coding agent at a repo, ask for a security audit, get verified findings.

Across the thread:
- [1/](https://x.com/wushi123321/status/2115641466693525894) It's a playbook, not a scanner — a 6-phase audit with separate sub-agents per job (~51.6k stars, +16k in a week, MIT, per his Oct 28 check).
- [2/](https://x.com/wushi123321/status/2115641566597615965) Recon builds a trust-boundary coverage ledger, isolated "hunters" work it, and a fresh agent tries to *disprove* each candidate; results land in a checked findings.json as confirmed / needs_validation / rejected.
- [3/](https://x.com/wushi123321/status/2115641616774074546) Limits: needs tool use and parallel sub-agents, a real sandbox to execute target code, burns tokens, and one run finds only about half of what repeated runs do; last commit was mid-September.
